rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so this experiment tests a baseline multimodal configuration (singleprofile, PCA+ResNet50, concat fusion) to establish whether combining modalities improves performance. It isolates the effect of multimodal fusion while using standard encoders, providing critical evidence to guide subsequent exploration or exploitation of more complex configurations.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, concat fusion) achieved 0.526 validation accuracy. This experiment tests the impact of switching from 'concat' to 'weighted' fusion while keeping other settings identical (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000 RNA, resnet50 image, no aggregation). This isolates the effect of fusion method, a critical design choice, and directly compares two common multimodal strategies. It balances exploitation (building on the prior multimodal approach) and exploration (testing a key variant).

Existing evidence shows that singleprofile with concat fusion achieves 0.526 accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion to isolate the effect of profile setting. It's the best next step as it explores a key design choice (profile setting) that could significantly impact performance, while keeping other factors (encoder, fusion) consistent for comparison.

The existing evidence shows that config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, avgpool, concat) achieves 0.6186 accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to weighted fusion (config_019) improves performance in the same setting, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It balances exploitation (building on the multiprofile success) and exploration (testing a key design choice).

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_019) achieve the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l (a more advanced architecture) further improves performance, isolating the effect of the image encoder while keeping other parameters consistent. This is a critical step to determine if upgrading the image encoder could yield better results, leveraging the current best setup without overcomplicating changes.

The existing evidence shows that multiprofile setups with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_019) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.639). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more sophisticated model) while keeping other components (multiprofile, avgpool, weighted fusion) the same could further improve performance. This clarifies the impact of RNA encoder choice on accuracy, building on the promising multiprofile framework.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (config_031) achieves high accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder with imagenet_vit_l (a stronger model) while maintaining the effective fusion and aggregation strategies can further improve performance. It directly addresses uncertainty about the optimal image encoder for multiprofile multimodal models.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_037) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.706). This experiment tests whether switching aggregation from avgpool to transformer while retaining weighted fusion could further improve performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. This is a logical extension of the current top-performing configuration and balances exploitation of promising components with exploration of a critical design choice.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_039) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.724989). This experiment tests whether replacing the scvi_n200 RNA encoder with scgpt (a newer encoder) in the same architecture could further improve performance. It isolates the effect of the RNA encoder while maintaining the proven effective components (transformer aggregation, weighted fusion, multiprofile), maximizing the chance to find a small but impactful improvement with the final experiment.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scgpt and imagenet_vit_l encoders, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests the same encoder and aggregation setup but uses concat fusion instead of weighted fusion, isolating the effect of fusion type. It is the best use of the final budget to validate if the fusion method is critical for performance, potentially confirming or improving upon the current best.
